questions.text: A hospital in the worst-performing quartile of hospitals nationally on Hospital-Acquired Condition measures will face which of the following financial consequences under the HACRP?

options.a: A 2% reduction on payments for only those discharges where the HAC occurred
options.b: A 1% reduction on ALL Medicare discharges regardless of where the HAC occurred
options.c: Mandatory enrollment in the Hospital Value-Based Purchasing Program
options.d: A 3% reduction applied only to surgical discharges

questions.explanation: A 1% reduction on ALL Medicare discharges regardless of where the HAC occurred The HACRP applies a 1% payment reduction to all Medicare discharges — not just those cases where the HAC occurred. This is the key distinction that makes HACRP financially impactful and a strong organizational motivator for system-wide safety culture.

questions.text: A physician group practice participates in MIPS under MACRA. In which of the following scenarios is the group most at risk for a negative payment adjustment?

options.a: They score above the performance threshold on all four MIPS categories
options.b: They submit data late and score below the performance threshold
options.c: They qualify as an Advanced APM participant and opt out of MIPS
options.d: They use a Qualified Clinical Data Registry (QCDR) for reporting

questions.explanation: They submit data late and score below the performance threshold MIPS scoring governs payment adjustments under MACRA — poor performance results in negative payment adjustments. Late submission reduces the score. Qualifying as an Advanced APM participant exempts a practice from MIPS entirely.

questions.text: Which of the following CAHPS instruments would be most appropriate for measuring patient experience in an emergency department setting?
questions.explanation: ED CAHPS ED CAHPS measures emergency department patient experience — specifically access, communication, and care coordination. HCAHPS measures inpatient hospital experience; CG-CAHPS measures outpatient clinic experience; HCBS CAHPS measures Medicaid home and community-based services.

questions.text: The Hospital Value-Based Purchasing Program (HVBP) uses a budget-neutral methodology. What does this mean in practice?

options.a: CMS funds incentive payments using additional appropriations from Congress
options.b: High-performing hospitals earn bonuses funded entirely by penalties withheld from lower performers
options.c: All hospitals receive equal payments regardless of performance under HVBP
options.d: HVBP payments are offset against HRRP penalties to create a net neutral effect

questions.explanation: High-performing hospitals earn bonuses funded entirely by penalties withheld from lower performers Incentive payments are funded by penalties captured from lower performers — making HVBP budget-neutral. CMS withholds up to 2% of base Medicare payments and redistributes them based on Total Performance Score.

questions.text: According to the IOM/HMD Six Domains of Healthcare Quality, a patient who receives a necessary medication that is evidence-based but must wait 4 hours for it to be administered has experienced a failure in which domain?
questions.explanation: Timely Timely is defined as reducing waits and harmful delays for both receiving and giving care. The medication is evidence-based (Effective domain met) and appropriate (Safe domain met) — but the 4-hour delay represents a failure in the Timely domain.
